narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Luke: narration, speech introductions and glosses.

peter.name: Peter
peter.note: Chief of the apostles; bold and plain-spoken, with authority.

angel.name: Angel of the Lord
angel.note: A messenger of God; brief, clear command.

crowd.name: People of Samaria
crowd.note: The Samaritans, awed by Simon the magician.

simon-magus.name: Simon the Magician
simon-magus.note: Samaritan sorcerer; grasping when he offers money, then frightened.

holy-spirit.name: The Holy Spirit
holy-spirit.note: The Spirit prompting Philip; quiet, direct.

philip-the-deacon.name: Philip the Deacon
philip-the-deacon.note: One of the seven, the evangelist (not the apostle); eager and friendly.

ethiopian-eunuch.name: The Ethiopian Eunuch
ethiopian-eunuch.note: Treasurer of queen Candace; courteous, earnest, joyful in asking for baptism.

1.t: And at that time, there was raised a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem. And they were all dispersed through the countries of Judea, and Samaria, except the apostles.

2.t: And devout men took order for Stephen's funeral and made great mourning over him.

3.t: But Saul made havock of the church, entering in from house to house: and dragging away men and women, committed them to prison.

4.t: They therefore that were dispersed went about preaching the word of God.

5.t: And Philip, going down to the city of Samaria, preached Christ unto them.

6.t: And the people with one accord were attentive to those things which were said by Philip, hearing, and seeing the miracles which he did.

7.t: For many of them who had unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, went out.

8.t: And many, taken with the palsy, and that were lame, were healed.

9.t: There was therefore great joy in that city. Now there was a certain man named Simon who before had been a magician in that city, seducing the people of Samaria, giving out that he was some great one:

10.t: To whom they all gave ear, from the least to the greatest, saying:
This man is the power of God, which is called great.

11.t: And they were attentive to him, because, for a long time, he had bewitched them with his magical practices.

12.t: But when they had believed Philip preaching of the kingdom of God, in the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

13.t: Then Simon himself believed also and, being baptized, he adhered to Philip. And being astonished, wondered to see the signs and exceeding great miracles which were done.

14.t: Now, when the apostles, who were in Jerusalem, had heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John.

15.t: Who, when they were come, prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost.

16.t: For he was not as yet come upon any of them: but they were only baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

17.t: Then they laid their hands upon them: and they received the Holy Ghost.

18.t: And when Simon saw that, by the imposition of the hands of the apostles, the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money,

19.t: Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I shall lay my hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost.

20.t: Keep thy money to thyself, to perish with thee: because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

21.t: Thou hast no part nor lot in this matter. For thy heart is not right in the sight of God.

22.t: Do penance therefore for this thy wickedness: and pray to God, that perhaps this thought of thy heart may be forgiven thee.

23.t: For I see thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bonds of iniquity.

24.t: Pray you for me to the Lord that none of these things which you have spoken may come upon me.

25.t: And they indeed, having testified and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem: and preached the gospel to many countries of the Samaritans.

26.t: Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying:
Arise, go towards the south, to the way that goeth down from Jerusalem into Gaza: this is desert.
26.q: "this is desert" may be Luke's own gloss on the road rather than the angel's words; kept with the angel.

27.t: And rising up, he went. And behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch, of great authority under Candace the queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge over all her treasures, had come to Jerusalem to adore.

28.t: And he was returning, sitting in his chariot and reading Isaias the prophet.

29.t: And the Spirit said to Philip:
Go near and join thyself to this chariot.

30.t: And Philip running thither, heard him reading the prophet Isaias. And he said:
Thinkest thou that thou understandest what thou readest?

31.t: And how can I, unless some man shew me?
And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.

32.t: And the place of the scripture which he was reading was this:
He was led as a sheep to the slaughter: and like a lamb without voice before his shearer, so openeth he not his mouth.
32.q: The Isaias passage the eunuch was reading aloud; treated as written text quoted by the narrator, not as his speech.

33.t: In humility his judgment was taken away. His generation who shall declare, for his life shall be taken from the earth?
33.q: Continuation of the Isaias passage; narrator, as in v. 32.

34.t: And the eunuch answering Philip, said:
I beseech thee, of whom doth the prophet speak this? Of himself, or of some other man?

35.t: Then Philip, opening his mouth and beginning at this scripture, preached unto him Jesus.

36.t: And as they went on their way, they came to a certain water. And the eunuch said:
See, here is water: What doth hinder me from being baptized?

37.t: If thou believest with all thy heart, thou mayest.
I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.

38.t: And he commanded the chariot to stand still. And they went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch. And he baptized him.

39.t: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord took away Philip: and the eunuch saw him no more. And he went on his way rejoicing.

40.t: But Philip was found in Azotus: and passing through, he preached the gospel to all the cities, till he came to Caesarea.
